newsitem.title: USA: Florida citrus belt stays dry, harvest increasing.
newsitem.headline: Florida citrus belt stays dry, harvest increasing.

text.p: Most areas of the Florida citrus belt were dry again for the week ended Nov 17, the Florida Agricultural Statistics Service (FASS) said, with most early fruit in good condition and showing very good progress.
Friday, Saturday, and Sunday were windy with gusts up to 45 mph near East Coast citrus growing areas, though harvest is increasing in all areas, FASS said.
According to FASS, caretakers are cutting cover crops that have grown tall and woody, applying very few sprays, and some growers are applying their pre-winter fertilizations.
Additionally, FASS estimated 225,000 boxes of navel oranges were harvested in the week ended November 17, down from 258,000 boxes in the previous week and 211,000 boxes in the week ended November 3.
An estimated 2,373,000 boxes of early and mid oranges were harvested in the week ended November 17, up from 2,037,000 boxes the prior week and 547,000 boxes the week ended November 3, FASS said.
